## 0f7d80015d9d

**A0F-1 — Reproduced coverage defect: a marker-order shortcut survives the entire generated support.** This is a findings-only audit; the target generator and all rule authorities remain unchanged. No generated wrong label or canonical rejection was found in the checks below.

Audited version **3.0.0**, generator SHA-256 **`f576456b685e460e55ddfcd13d3554b45e6b391505bf80e7e4a3a618e23a7e8f`**, selected/executed rule hash **`9744dc525afc`**. The supported Racket receipt records executed rule-text SHA-256 **`383a8eb2b190368237a757ed755017885b247d94d29ef7a5479967fe476993e7`**. All counts here refer to those unchanged source bytes.

### Finding and mechanism

The plausible rival moves red to cyan as usual, then stamps the new cyan beside the rectangle's bottom on the **right iff the original red column is less than the original cyan column**, otherwise on the left. This rule never computes the rectangle midpoint. It fits **all 4/4 usable canonical pairs**, covering the three training pairs and the test pair in the single canonical variant.

Every generated profile makes this comparison equivalent to the intended red-versus-midpoint comparison. Let `r`, `c`, and `m` denote red column, cyan column, and integer rectangle midpoint:

| Generated profile | Relationship enforced by `generate` | `r < c` | Intended `r < m` |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `left_opposite` | `r < m < c` | True | True |
| `right_opposite` | `c < m < r` | False | False |
| `center_opposite` | `c < r = m` | False | False |
| `right_same_side` | `c = m < r` | False | False |

The last profile always sets cyan exactly at the midpoint. Its name and same-side witness therefore do not distinguish marker ordering from red's side relative to the rectangle. These four branches exhaust `generate`; seeds, difficulties and accepted public overrides cannot break the equivalence. This is a source-level support argument, supplemented by the sampled results below, rather than an inference of universal coverage from a finite sample.

### Small, authority-verified separator and domain status

The retained hand-constructed **9×9** input has a solid gray rectangle at rows **5–8**, columns **1–6**, red at **(4,4)** and cyan at **(4,5)**, using zero-based coordinates. Its midpoint is column **3**. Both markers are strictly to the right of the midpoint, while red is left of cyan.

Both `self_check(input)` and `strict_canonical_like(input)` return **`[]`**. It obeys the documented `INVARIANTS`, is recognized as `right_same_side`, and has the canonical-linked geometry `(9,9,4,6)`. However, it is **outside actual sampler support**, because `generate` can only put cyan at column 3 in that profile. It is a hand-input separator: there is no generation seed or sample index for it.

The selected Racket authority erases red at `(4,4)`, recolors cyan at `(4,5)` red, and stamps cyan at **(8,0)**. The rival makes the same first two changes but stamps cyan at **(8,7)**. Full input, actual Racket output, rival output, source identity and domain annotations are in [evidence.json](checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/evidence.json), `counterexample`. It is input/result **index 4** in the supported [Racket receipt](checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/racket.json).

This reproduces a gap between the stated and validator-accepted task domain and the sampler's teaching coverage. It does **not** demonstrate a wrong generated label or a rival failure on the current generated distribution; the rival survives that distribution.

### Checks actually run

| Check | Selection and denominator | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Canonical acceptance and rival fit | All 4 usable canonical pairs | Validator and strict predicate accept 4/4; mirror and new rival match 4/4 canonical outputs. |
| Default generated support | Seeds `0,1,17,2026`; sample indices `0..63`; difficulty `None,easy,medium,hard`; no overrides | 1,024/1,024 valid inputs; rival matches Python mirror 1,024/1,024; **940 unique inputs**. |
| Exact override boundaries | All 4 difficulties × heights `{7,19}` × widths `{7,19}` × 3 declared aspects × 4 declared profiles; case `0..191`, seed `41000+case`, index `case` | All axes observed exactly and validator accepts 192/192; rival matches mirror 192/192; **192 unique inputs**. No ignored control found in this boundary probe. |
| Full schedule starts | Seed `17`; all 4 difficulties; raw starts `0..15`; four consecutive demos followed by one query | 64/64 direct windows pass `lesson_identifiable` and refute every declared competitor; the new rival fits every demo and query in all 64. **320 overlapping input occurrences, 72 unique inputs**. These are direct raw windows, not independent production lessons. |
| Racket authority comparison | 4 canonical inputs + hand separator + seed `17`, indices `0..11`, all 4 difficulties, no overrides | 53/53 results have valid outputs and no runtime errors; mirror agrees with Racket 53/53. Rival agrees on all 4 canonical and all 48 generated results (**44 unique generated inputs**), and disagrees on the hand separator. |

The probe iterates the actual `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` and `LESSON_COMPETITORS` declarations. The sole declared canonical shortcut, `center_is_left`, fits all 4/4 canonical pairs; every declared competitor is refuted in all 64 sampled four-demo windows. The new marker-order rival is absent from those declarations. The 1,024 default and 192 override counts use the Python mirror; only the explicitly identified 53 results were independently executed in Racket.

Exact selections, per-sample hashes, validator outcomes and declaration checks are retained in [preliminary.json](checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/preliminary.json). The reusable [probe.py](checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/probe.py) invokes only public authoring helpers and the supported CLI. Actual commands, working directories and exit statuses are in [commands.json](checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/commands.json). Both the full probe and supported authority command exited **0**:

```text
cwd: packet_root
python3 checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/probe.py

cwd: packet_root; wrapper payload cwd: repo
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 0f7d80015d9d --input ../checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/input.json --out ../checks/audit/0f7d80015d9d/racket.json
```

**Suggested task-local follow-up:** add this rival to the canonical shortcut and lesson competitor declarations, and provide recurring same-side scenes with cyan farther right than red, while preserving the existing decisive profiles. Recheck complete lessons after any schedule change. No repair is included for this audit-only target.
